message.reasoning:
I need to decide whether to pay the $50 jail fine or roll for doubles.

I rolled doubles at turn 114 but stayed in jail. I will roll for doubles again rather than pay the $50 fine.

Staying in jail is safer. I have $254 cash and an orange monopoly with two houses each. Indiana is mortgaged against p3, who holds all four railroads and pinks at four houses each. p4 has Park Place and Boardwalk with one house on Boardwalk. p2 lacks a light blue monopoly.

p2 owns the yellow monopoly but has mortgaged Marvin Gardens, so they cannot build there. Leaving jail would land me on St Charles, Electric, States, Virginia, Penn RR, and St James. The pinks at four houses each charge very high rent.

Rolling from jail lands on St Charles for $750, States for $750, or Virginia for $800. The mortgaged Electric Company would not charge rent.

Rolling doubles from jail lands on Penn RR for $200 or St James for me. The pinks are the biggest danger: rolls 2, 4, and 5 all hit them, giving roughly a 22% chance of instant death-level rent. Paying the $50 fine would leave me with only $204, which cannot cover $750 in rent. Selling six orange houses would return about $300, but that still falls short of the required amount.

Mortgaging the orange properties would return $280, but that would destroy the monopoly and leave me broke. Rolling doubles from jail carries a one-in-six chance of escaping immediately. A 1-1 roll lands on St Charles for $750, a 2-2 roll lands on States for $750, and a 3-3 roll lands on my own St James Place. A 4-4 roll lands on Community Chest.

Only 1-1 and 2-2 doubles are dangerous. A 5-5 roll lands on New York, and a 6-6 roll lands on Illinois, both safe. The chance of a catastrophic exit is only about 5.6 percent. If I fail again, I will have two jail turns and must pay the fine on the third attempt.
